input.rationale: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose parallel, mutual caps at the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid in the twelve months preceding accrual of the first claim, so the mutuality and 12-months-of-fees fallback elements are met, and indemnification payments sit outside the cap as a separate limb (9.1(a)/9.2(a)). Section 10 also excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually. However, there is no carve-out anywhere for breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or willful misconduct; indeed § 6 expressly subordinates the confidentiality regime to Sections 5, 9 and 10 for information in the hosting environment, so confidentiality breaches are capped. That fails the fallback on three material terms, so we have added a single mutual carve-out sentence as new Section 9.3. Noted but not separately flagged at fallback level: the cap floor is $100,000 rather than USD 1,000,000, there are no carve-outs for fraud or IP infringement, Customer's payment obligations are not expressly excluded from capped damages, and § 9.1(c)(2) disclaims all IBM liability for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data — all preferred-level points we would pursue if the carve-out sentence is accepted.

proposal.summary: Add mutual carve-out from the Section 9 liability limits for breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and willful misconduct.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The mutual caps in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 are acceptable at our fallback (twelve months' charges, with indemnification payments already outside the cap), but our position requires confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and willful misconduct to sit outside the limits for both parties. We have added one short mutual carve-out sentence rather than reopening Section 9.

ops.text: The limitations and exclusions of liability in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 do not apply to a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, its gross negligence or its willful misconduct.
